title: Canonical marketplace registry index
description: The canonical registry (spec 10846). Marketplace-first FM-1 rates the index a single point of TOTAL failure -- one malformed entry unresolves every package -- so the index is (a) itself signed, (b) validated before any entry is read, and (c) never partially applied: `mkt.index.load` either returns a fully validated index or raises. `entries` is a flat list of (name, version) coordinates; there is no per-name nesting because a nested shape lets the same version appear twice under different parents.

permissions.description: MIRRORED from the manifest so a client can refuse on permissions BEFORE fetching a payload. The linter asserts index.permissions == manifest.permissions exactly; a mirror that widens the manifest here is the cheapest possible supply-chain attack and MKT-L07 is the check that sees it.

yanked.description: A yank hides a version from RESOLUTION but leaves an explicit pin installable. Revocation (revocation.schema.json) blocks both. Two verbs, two strengths, no overlap.

revocation_path.description: Where the revocation list lives, relative to the registry root. REQUIRED in practice by mkt.install: if this key is absent, or the file it names is missing/unparseable, every install REFUSES. Fail-closed, because a revocation channel that can be removed to re-enable a revoked package is not a revocation channel.

signature.description: Signature over the canonical form of this document with `signature` removed, by the registry maintainer key declared in trust-policy.schema.json.
